expected_blocks.source: Field Measurement and Record Guide
A flowing fictional handbook for checking numeric records and field notes.
Site Preparation

During cycle 100, the north team at Alder reviewed 3 245 000 records. The mean reading was 8.93, while a separate tray held 3,500 samples. Two repeat checks returned 8.93, and a later reader also recorded 8.93. The team kept a 3-D frame, a 4-m shelf, and a 6-CD case beside the 20-yr copy.

In 2025, the river station compared 4 500 000 entries with 4,200 control pieces. A reading of 0.7 matched the earlier 8.93 result, and the second 8.93 check stayed within range. Labels 3b, 3B, and 3k remain distinct. The notes also compare 4.b, 4.B, and 4.m before approving a 3-dimensional gauge.

The Cedar register lists 1 234 567 observations from cycle 102. Its decimal sample is .7, and the comma-marked batch contains 12,750 pieces. Staff verified a 4-m support, a 6-CD archive, and a 20-yr record before repeating the 3-D inspection. The repeated value 8.93 appears twice so readers can compare the two entries.
The date 1947 08 31 and time 16 00 are sample fields. ISBN 978 1 55468 513 4 and phone 61 3 1234 5678 use numeric spaces when the record context is clear.

A 4th review checks the archive log for 8 765 432 items and a 4.2 reading. Another batch contains 975,000 samples. The calibration sheet keeps 3-D, 4-m, and 6-CD labels in their original order, while a 20yr summary and a 3-dimensional diagram provide near-neighbor examples for training.

For the East report, the team counted 2 048 000 records, checked 6,400 items, and repeated the value 8.93. The comparison reading was 8.93 again, with a decimal sample of 17.26. A 3-D panel, a 4-m shelf, and a 6-CD box protect the 20-yr copy during the next 1st review.
